transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

It is hard to say if the heater has failed without more info, as wet clothes are often caused by simple issues like overloading or blocked airflow rather than a broken part. The most common cause is putting a full wash load straight into dry, which exceeds the machine's drying capacity and leaves things damp even if the heat works. Another frequent culprit is restricted airflow from fluff in the filter or condenser, which stops moisture from escaping efficiently. Please unplug the machine first, then check the pump filter at the bottom front for any blockages of lint or debris. Also, please confirm how large the load was compared to the drum size, as drying more than about half the wash capacity typically results in poor drying.
It was a full 9kg drum, washed and dried in one go. The manual says 6kg dry capacity for drying. I haven't checked the pump filter yet, will do that.

That suggests why it didn't dry well, as putting 9kg into a 6kg dry cycle is too much for the condenser to handle effectively. Since you are checking the filter now, please also look at the condenser unit which is usually located behind that same flap or just above the filter housing. You can pull this out carefully and rinse it under warm water to remove any hidden fluff or scale buildup. Cleaning both of these will restore proper airflow and ensure moisture is condensed correctly during the next cycle.
Ok, will do. Should I be drying a smaller load then? I've also been turning the spin down to 800 on most washes, in case that matters.

Yes, you should most likely dry a smaller load than what you wash to ensure it dries properly. Please try running a cycle with a smaller load and set the spin speed to its highest appropriate level next time you use it.
